77f79941b4.q: What are the four phases of healthy feedback framework in Firm Feedback in a Fragile World?
77f79941b4.a: Jeff Hancher outlines four phases: phase one is building relationship through one-on-one meetings to understand what's important to people and their strengths; phase two is setting clear expectations; phase three is the ongoing feedback dialogue such as individual development plans and sales plan references; and phase four is accountability, which leaders earn the right to deliver only after establishing the first three pillars.

7ad3537d70.q: Why is directive feedback essential for new employee onboarding in sales teams?
7ad3537d70.a: Directive feedback should be used for new hires because they don't know what they don't know, even if they are industry experts or experienced salespeople. Directive feedback provides the support and validation needed, builds confidence, and bridges the productivity gap that new hires create. This strong foundation prevents the irresponsibility of asking a new hire on day one what they would like to do, when proper onboarding requires directing them through company processes and sales methodology.

5499d2199c.q: How should sales leaders deliver feedback in real-time field scenarios beyond one-on-one meetings?
5499d2199c.a: Sales leaders should understand the three types of feedback—directive, supportive, and collaborative—and know when each is appropriate. Supportive feedback works for high performers who are in a valley, requiring leaders to ask good questions to uncover personal issues or what might be affecting performance. Collaborative feedback suits experienced salespeople. The key is showing up in the field through ride-alongs and market visits rather than remaining behind a desk, allowing leaders to witness real-time performance and deliver feedback tactfully in context.

0000a4d76d.q: What percentage of the time should directive feedback be used in leadership conversations?
0000a4d76d.a: Directive feedback should typically be used less than 20% of the time. It is most appropriate in two specific situations: when there is an impending event involving safety or lack of time (such as a critical fourth-and-one moment with no time left), and when onboarding a brand new employee who needs clear company-specific guidance.

5b3acedab1.q: What did succession planning data reveal about why leaders fail to advance in Fortune 500 companies?
5b3acedab1.a: Jeff Hancher reviewed seven years of succession planning notes from his senior corporate role and found that hundreds of non-promotable leaders lacked two key qualities: emotional intelligence, and the ability to challenge in a healthy way or give feedback and accountability that people actually valued. Leaders who lack these skills may appear bold in their directness but fail to be effective, which keeps them from advancement.
